name: Centro
tagline: The rebuilt centre between the bay and the cathedral
description: Santander's core, reconstructed after the 1941 fire, running from the port and the Centro Botin along the bay to the cathedral and the market. Shops, offices, the pintxo bars and the ferry terminal all sit here, and the waterfront promenade starts at the door.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the bay, the market and the pintxo bars within a short walk
pros: Bay promenade and the Botin gallery on the doorstep
The best rental supply and all bus routes
Pintxo bars and the covered market close by
cons: Rents at the top of the local market
Twentieth century architecture rather than an old town
Busy and noisy on summer evenings

name: El Sardinero
tagline: The beach district, with the casino and the long promenade
description: The seaside quarter on the northern side of the peninsula, built around two long sand beaches, the Belle Epoque casino and a promenade that runs the length of them. It is where Santander goes in summer and where the best-positioned flats are, at prices to match the sea view.
bestFor: Stays built around swimming, surfing and a walk on the promenade before work
pros: Two long beaches and the promenade immediately there
Quieter and greener than the centre
Surf schools and the Magdalena peninsula nearby
cons: The most expensive rents in the city in summer
Twenty-five minutes on foot to the centre
Very busy in July and August

name: Cuatro Caminos and Valdenoja
tagline: The everyday districts, where residents live and rents are sane
description: The residential belt west and north of the centre around the Cuatro Caminos junction, with apartment blocks, local markets, schools and the bus network. It has no sea view and no old town, which is precisely why a flat here costs meaningfully less than the same thing near the beach.
bestFor: Longer stays where the rent matters more than the address
pros: Rents well below the centre and Sardinero
Full local shopping, markets and services
cons: No sea view and little character
Fifteen to twenty minutes from the beaches

name: Peninsula de la Magdalena and Somo Ferry Side
tagline: The park end of the bay, with the palace and the crossing to Somo
description: The eastern tip of the city where the Magdalena palace sits in a public park on its own headland, with small coves below and the ferry across the bay to the surf beaches at Somo. Quiet, green and residential, with the park functioning as the city's back garden.
bestFor: Quiet stays with the park, the coves and the ferry to the surf
pros: The Magdalena park and its coves on the doorstep
Ferry to the long surf beach at Somo
cons: Half an hour on foot to the centre
High rents for what is available

name: Puertochico
tagline: The small harbour between the centre and Sardinero
description: The old fishing harbour on the bay, now a marina ringed by seafood restaurants and terraces, sitting neatly between the commercial centre and the beaches. It has the best eating in the city per square metre and a position that makes both ends of Santander a short walk away.
bestFor: Anyone whose priority is the seafood and the terraces on the water
pros: The best concentration of restaurants in the city
Halfway between the centre and the beaches
